content.user_title: Keep Next.js and Astro Changes Server-First
content.value_statement: UI changes can introduce unnecessary browser code and inconsistent component boundaries. This skill guides framework detection, server-first implementation, explicit data states, and documented boundary decisions.
actual_capabilities: Identify Next.js or Astro from dependencies and root configuration files, and request clarification when signals conflict.
Keep Next.js client components limited to leaves requiring state, effects, event handlers, or browser APIs.
Prefer server-rendered Astro components and small interactive islands with the least eager hydration directive that works.
Reuse existing components, shadcn primitives, semantic tokens, and project design guidance.
Require explicit loading, empty, and error states and tests proportional to the change risk.
Report the detected framework, boundary changes, reasons, and completion checklist answers.
limitations: Framework-specific guidance covers Next.js and Astro, not other application frameworks.
This is an instruction skill, not a bundled compiler, test runner, or automatic architecture enforcement tool.
Implementation depends on access to project files, installed framework documentation, and existing quality tooling.
Design guidance and companion skills apply only when available; the skill does not install them.

use_cases.title: Add an Interactive Next.js Component
use_cases.description: Keep page rendering and data fetching on the server while isolating a small interactive component.

use_cases.title: Choose Astro Island Boundaries
use_cases.description: Separate static content from interactive widgets and select hydration directives based on interaction needs.

use_cases.title: Review UI Architecture Changes
use_cases.description: Check framework evidence, design consistency, data states, and reasons for new client boundaries before closing a change.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-architecture to inspect this project and identify its framework. Report the evidence and ask for clarification if it is ambiguous.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the project before requesting UI changes.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Small UI Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-architecture to add an empty state to this data display. Follow existing design conventions and report any server/client boundary changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: make a focused UI improvement.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Minimal Interactive Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-architecture to add a filter to this list. Keep rendering server-first, isolate necessary interaction, and test loading, empty, and error states.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: introduce interaction without expanding client code unnecessarily.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Broad Client Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-architecture to refactor this page for server-first rendering. Explain each boundary change, preserve behavior, and run reviewed project quality checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: restructure existing UI while preserving behavior.

output_examples.input: Add a collapsible details panel to a Next.js page.
output: Framework: Next.js, identified from project dependencies.
Boundary change: only the details toggle needs client state; the page and data fetching remain server-rendered.
Checklist: client code is limited to the interaction, existing design conventions are preserved, and applicable data states are explicit.

output_examples.input: Add an interactive calculator below static content in an Astro page.
output: Framework: Astro, identified from project configuration.
Boundary change: add one small React island for calculator input; surrounding content remains server-rendered.
Hydration: use visibility-based hydration because the calculator is below the initial viewport.
Checklist: no other client boundary is added; styling follows project guidance; applicable loading, empty, and error states are explicit.

best_practices: Confirm the target framework and consult documentation matching the installed version before changing framework APIs.
Keep interaction boundaries small and pass serializable props from server-rendered parents.
Review project quality scripts before running them, then document boundary reasons and checklist results.
anti_patterns: Marking an entire page as client-rendered when only one small control needs interaction.
Hydrating every Astro island immediately without evaluating visibility or idle hydration.
Creating custom components before checking existing primitives, semantic tokens, and project design guidance.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It provides specific architecture guidance for Next.js and Astro.

faq.question: How does it identify the framework?
faq.answer: It checks dependencies and root configuration files. If both frameworks appear or neither is detected, it asks which app the change targets.

faq.question: Does it prohibit client-side JavaScript?
faq.answer: No. It allows client code for necessary interaction and keeps the client boundary as small as possible.

faq.question: Does it require shadcn or companion skills?
faq.answer: It prioritizes existing shadcn primitives and loads companion skills when installed. It does not include an installation workflow.

faq.question: Does it run project checks?
faq.answer: The workflow requests an installed evaluation skill or project quality scripts. Review scripts before execution because project-defined commands can run code.

faq.question: What should the final report include?
faq.answer: The detected framework, every server/client boundary added or moved, the reason for each change, and checklist answers.
